qual_reasons:
  expression:
    clarity: Clear, correct IRS instructional prose; concrete terms; no banned register
      or trite phrasing; reads at publication standard for the genre.
    coherence: Sections progress logically; each paragraph has one job; transitions
      and Tip/Caution blocks bridge cleanly.
    concision: Each section earns its place; no padding or replacement-history; reference
      content carries only required rules.
  form:
    consistency: Consistent American style, dollar/date formats, acronym casing, parallel
      lists, citation conventions throughout.
    formatting: Markup mostly clean, but a stray escaped line break leaves '519.'
      / 'Form 8814\.' / '2025\.' line-break artifacts in rendered prose (F3 rule 6).
    organization: Well-arranged charts/headings, but several cross-references are
      bare pointers ('see Pub. 519', 'see Form 4868') without naming the target content
      (F1 rule 7).
  grounding:
    factuality: Verifiable claims (forms, pubs, statutory citations, links) resolve
      to real IRS artifacts; thresholds match the 2025 Form 1040 instructions source;
      no invented sources.
    relevance: Every section and citation bears directly on the filing-requirement
      purpose; no performative or tangential sourcing.
    verifiability: Claims trace to named IRS publications, forms, statute sections,
      and linked tax topics; thresholds are specific and checkable against the cited
      source instructions.
  judgment:
    calibration: NA — the document makes no probability, forecast, or confidence claims;
      filing thresholds are categorical rules, not estimates.
    fairness: NA — a normative filing-requirements reference surfaces no oppositional
      framings and the task does not call for them.
    robustness: NA — the document makes no interpretive judgments admitting alternative
      lenses; it states authoritative filing rules.
  purpose:
    breadth: Covers citizens, resident/nonresident/dual-status aliens, dependents,
      extensions, PDS, special-tax situations; relevant case classes within scope
      present.
    depth: Thresholds quantified to the dollar; conditions enumerated with named forms
      and instances; depth matches a filing-reference's stakes.
    scope: Scope (2025 Form 1040/1040-SR filing requirements) clear from title/frontmatter
      but never stated as a one-line boundary in the body opening (P2 rule 1); minor
      slip.
    suitability: Task (when/whether you must file) is named; Charts A/B/C answer it;
      output shape (rule reference) matches a reference-doc task; main answers recoverable
      from headings.
  reasoning:
    discipline: NA — content is a normative/imperative reference (filing rules and
      definitions); it states requirements rather than reasoning from observations
      up the inference ladder.
    parsimony: NA — Soundness engages but the document makes no inferential reasoning
      chains (it states rules); per the Discipline NA basis there is no chain whose
      minimality could be evaluated.
    precision: Specific statute sections (965, 965(h/i)), named forms, dated thresholds,
      and proper entity names used throughout; no vague placeholders.
    soundness: Terms (gross/earned/unearned income) defined where load-bearing; conditions
      internally consistent; no causal mechanism claims to misstate.

1. **Scope** (rule 1) *[partial]* — Scope (2025 1040/1040-SR filing requirements) lives
   in frontmatter/title but is never declared as an explicit boundary in the body
   opening. *Location:*
   `"These rules apply to all U.S. citizens, regardless of where they live, and resident aliens."`
   Filing Requirements.
2. **Organization** (rule 7) *[partial]* — Cross-references are bare pointers that don’t
   name the target content (e.g., ‘See Pub.
   519 for details’). *Location:*
   `"Generally, you are a resident alien if you meet either the green card test or the substantial presence test for 2025. See Pub. 519 for details."`
   Resident aliens.
3. **Formatting** (rule 6) *[partial]* — Escaped trailing line-break artifacts leak into
   rendered prose (e.g., ‘Form 8814.’ and ‘$25,000 … 2025.’). *Location:* `"8814\."`
   Exception for certain children under age 19 or full-time students; `"2025\."` Chart
   A--For Most People.
